rules.name: Methodology Requirement
rules.desc:
Methodology courses should be selected based on their potential to support the student’s projected capstone project.
Methodology courses must be taken for 3-5 units and a letter grade.
rules.notes: Note that Methodology courses may not be offered every year. For an up-to-date list of this academic year's Methodology courses, visit the Core Coursework page on the CCSRE website.

rules.name: International Dimension
rules.desc: Asian American Studies majors must complete one International Dimension course that explores issues of race and ethnicity outside of the United States.
rules.notes: Note that International Dimension courses may not be offered every year. For an up-to-date list of this academic year's International Dimension courses, visit the Core Coursework page on the CCSRE website.

rules.name: Community-Engaged Learning Requirement
rules.desc: CCSRE students must complete at least one Community-Engaged Learning (CEL) course or co-curricular experience that centers issues of race, ethnicity, and inequality. This requirement may be fulfilled by enrolling in a Cardinal Course, completing a CCSRE Undergraduate Fellowship, or participating in an Alternative Spring Break. The CEL requirement may be fulfilled by courses that also fulfill other Asian American Studies degree requirements (e.g., a Methodology course may also count toward the CEL requirement). The CEL requirement may be fulfilled by academic experiences, such as fellowships, that do not carry academic units.
rules.notes: See the Community-Engaged Learning course list on the Core Coursework page on the CCSRE website for this year's curricular offerings.

rules.name: Asian American Studies Electives (toward the 60 units)
rules.desc:
Asian American Studies majors must complete the remaining units of their 60-unit minimum with elective coursework in Asian American Studies. Exceptions are listed below.

• Asian American Studies majors may count up to 8 units of Department of African and African American Studies (DAAAS), Chicana/o-Latina/o Studies (CHILATST), Comparative Studies in Race and Ethnicity (CSRE), Jewish Studies (JEWISHST), or Native American Studies (NATIVEAM) courses toward their degree in Asian American Studies.

• Asian American Studies majors may count up to 5 units of advanced study of an Asian language (see below) toward the major degree.

rules.name: Language Study (optional)
rules.desc: Students may apply for credit studying an Asian language toward their degree. If students complete 15 or more units of advanced (second-year or beyond) Asian language study, they may apply 5 of those units toward their Asian American Studies major.

rules.name: Writing in the Major (WIM)
rules.notes:
CCSRE students must plan to complete 200X or 201X in person on Stanford campus in autumn of their final year of study.

Note that the same five-unit course fulfills the WIM and Capstone requirements.

rules.name: Honors

children.name: Honors thesis graded B+ or above, from an approved proposal
GPA of 3.7 in the major and 3.5 overall, kept until graduation

rules.desc:
Honors students must apply with a complete proposal approved by a CCSRE faculty advisor in the spring preceding their final year of study. Honors students must continuously enroll at Stanford in autumn, winter, and spring. For more information about the Honors program and the application process, visit the Honors page on the CCSRE website.

Honors applications are open to students with a grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.7 in the major and 3.5 overall. Students must receive a grade of B+ or above on their thesis and maintain the GPA minimum until graduation in order to receive Honors.
rules.notes: A minimum grade of C- is required for a student to count a class towards the Core Curriculum, including the WIM and Capstone requirements.

grading: All courses must be taken for a letter grade, unless only offered S/NC. A minimum grade of C- is required for a student to count a class towards the Core Curriculum, including the Gateway, Comparative Core, Major Core, Methodology, International Dimension, WIM, and Capstone requirements. Additional units toward the major require a passing grade of D- or above. Student may count 2 classes with Satisfactory/No Credit (SNC) grading basis toward Additional Units.
policies:
Course Petition Policy
No more than 15 units of petitioned courses that are not listed under CCSRE or cross-listed with CCSRE may be applied to the Asian American Studies major. Students who wish to petition a course must fill out and submit a course petition form for the CCSRE Academic Programs team to review within one month of completing their annual degree audit meeting with the CCSRE Student Services Officer.
transferPolicy: Up to 20 units of external credit may be applied toward elective coursework in the major.
reviewNotes: The audit counts your courses toward the 60 units the major needs. Every core course (gateway, comparative core, major core, methodology, international dimension, community-engaged learning, WIM and capstone) must be taken for a letter grade, unless only offered S/NC, with a C- or better; methodology courses need 3 or more units. The rest of the 60 units are ASNAMST electives, plus at most 8 units of AFRICAAM, CHILATST, CSRE, JEWISHST or NATIVEAM courses and 5 units of Asian language. Petitioned courses (at most 15 units), external credit (at most 20 units) and a CEL fellowship or Alternative Spring Break are moved in by hand. Left: you may count only 2 electives taken S/NC, which the audit does not limit. Honors requires CSRE 201X-Z, a B+ thesis and the GPA minimums.
